summary: Initial discovery focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency needs, streaming vs. non-streaming tradeoffs, and benchmarking approach (tokens/sec). Elysium currently evaluating hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for PHI-adjacent bio annotations. Key asks: p95 < 300ms for short generation (<=128 tokens), sustained 200 QPS with streaming, clear security posture (SOC2, KMS), and a reproducible benchmark run on their prompts.
topics: deployment tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick us off. quick agenda: latency targets, concurrency, streaming, and a proposed benchmark.
[00:12] Dr. Patel: Hi, thanks. we mainly care about latency for short clinical annotations basically under 128 tokens, and we have two modes: realtime clinician assist and batch enrichment. p95 is most important.
[00:28] Priya: got it. can you share your p95 target numbers and expected concurrency?
[00:33] Dr. Patel: for realtime, p95 we'd like under 300ms ideally, at 50 concurrent sessions. for background batch, throughput matters more; we want to sustain about 200QPS when needed for nightly enrichment.
[00:47] Carlos: just to add, we do streaming in the UI, so token per second and chunk latency matters – we don't want first token lag.
[00:55] Jordan: makes sense. so two buckets: low-latency streaming for interactive, and high-throughput for batch. our hosted API can do streaming with small first-byte times, but p95 at sub-300ms depends on model and request size.
[01:10] Priya: quick note, sometimes auto-transcript messes names, but technical: p95 is sensitive to batch sizes, kv cache warm state, and whether you're using dedicated GPUs or shared.
[01:22] Dr. Patel: what's the difference we'd see between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for p95? like ballpark numbers?
[01:30] Priya: Hosted (multi-tenant) for smaller models and low-fanout can hit 200-400ms p95 on optimized open models, but it varies. Dedicated reserved pools give more predictable tail latency — less noisy noisy neighbors — so you'd see more stable sub-300ms p95 at your concurrency. Private (VPC/on-prem) adds network hops and customer infra variability; if you colocate near clients it's fine but you take on ops.
[01:52] Samir: and cost tradeoffs?
[01:54] Jordan: right, Dedicated is pricier due to reserved capacity but predictable. Hosted is usage-based cheaper to start. For your 50 concurrent realtime users with sub-300ms p95, Dedicated might be recommended if you want predictable SLOs without constant tuning.
[02:10] Aisha: security question: we handle PHI-ish notes, what does Redwood provide for encryption and key management?
[02:16] Jordan: SOC2, customer-managed KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated, audit logs in Console. We'll share security whitepaper. For Hosted we offer encryption at rest and in transit and SOC2 compliance, but some customers require Private for full KMS control.
[02:32] Dr. Patel: ok, benchmark plan — how do we measure tokens/sec? we need something reproducible across models.
[02:38] Priya: good question. tokens/sec is measured downstream as output tokens divided by elapsed generation time; for streaming we'd measure first-byte latency and steady-state token emission rate. We usually run p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end latency and report tokens/sec per-request and aggregate concurrency throughput (requests/sec * avg tokens).
[02:57] Carlos: do you support on-the-fly quantized models or do you recommend certain quantization for throughput?
[03:02] Priya: we support quantized variants and have quantization profiles we recommend per workload. 4-bit on certain models improves tokens/sec but may affect quality. Redwood Optimize can suggest the profile based on your eval set.
[03:16] Jordan: also mention KV cache helps when you have repeated context (chat) and reduces per-token compute, improving tokens/sec for long sessions.
[03:24] Dr. Patel: do you have an example benchmark for 128-token generation p95 numbers?
[03:29] Priya: off the cuff, on a dedicated A100-like pool with an optimized LlamaX-style model you might see p95 ~180-250ms for 128-token generations single-turn, but depends on model weights, sequence length, and whether you're streaming. On-hosted for same model maybe 220-400ms p95 variegated.
[03:47] Samir: we want to run a reproducible 1-week test on our prompts, can Redwood run hosted benchmarks on our sample set?
[03:53] Jordan: yes, we can run a Redwood-hosted benchmark simulating your concurrency and tokens, measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, failure rates. We'll need your sample prompts and expected distribution.
[04:05] Carlos: what's the instrumentation? do you provide per-token timing and traces?
[04:08] Priya: Console provides per-route latency breakdown, token-level cost breakdown, and tracing hooks; we can export logs. For private deployments you can also forward audit logs to your SIEM.
[04:20] Dr. Patel: and fallback behavior? if a model tier is overloaded, do you have auto-fallback to a cheaper model?
[04:25] Jordan: yes, smart routing supports fallback policies by latency/cost/region and automatic fallbacks to compatible variants. You can pin critical endpoints to Dedicated.
[04:33] Dr. Patel: one more, concurrency spikes — say sudden 2x burst to 100 sessions — how do you handle?
[04:38] Priya: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity; Hosted has pooled burst but not guaranteed. For strict SLOs, Dedicated + reserved burst buffer recommended. Also batching settings and continuous batching can smooth spikes.
[04:50] Samir: do you expose tokens/sec in the billing or is it only tokens and time?
[04:55] Jordan: billing is tokens and unit charges; we surface tokens/sec and latency metrics in Console for optimization but charge per token. Redwood Optimize gives suggestions to reduce tokens while preserving quality.
[05:06] Carlos: about streaming: what's the typical first-byte latency we can expect?
[05:10] Priya: first-byte often smaller than full completion p95; in optimized runs we've seen first-byte ~40-120ms on dedicated infra for very short prompts. Again depends on model and network.
[05:20] Dr. Patel: sounds promising. for PHI, Private seems likely but we want to proof Hosted first to validate models and latency.
[05:26] Jordan: totally reasonable — do a hosted benchmark to validate quality and latency, then consider Dedicated pilot or Private for compliance.
[05:34] Carlos: timeline — we aim to pilot in Q2.
[05:37] Jordan: notes on deliverables: we'll send pricing/security docs, draft benchmark plan, and schedule deep dive.
[05:43] Priya: any other technical constraints (latency budgets inside clinic app)?
[05:46] Dr. Patel: yes, 250ms for first token ideally, cumulative completions under 300ms p95 for the common flows. If those numbers don't hold we'll need to rethink tradeoffs.
[05:59] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up.
[06:02] -- End --
